newsitem.title: USA: Chinese city Shenyang mulls issuing yankee bonds.
newsitem.headline: Chinese city Shenyang mulls issuing yankee bonds.

text.p: Shenyang, a major industrial city in northeast China, may be the first Chinese municipality to issue bonds in the United States, said Mayor Mu Suixin on Tuesday.
In an interview with Reuters, Mu said he has been in contact with U.S. investment banks regarding the debt issuance, while the city seeks approval from Beijing.

"We want to take the lead in offering Chinese municipal bonds to international investors," he said, adding that other countries, notably Russia, have successfully tapped this source of funding for regional development.
The capital raised would be put in a "Shenyang development fund" to reinvigorate the city's industrial complex, he said.
In his first visit to the United States since taking office in February, Mu spelled out an ambitious plan to attract foreign capital, technology and managerial skills.

Shenyang has a well developed transportation network and infrastructure for heavy industry, whose potentials await development with the help of international capital and world-class management, he told U.S. business leaders earlier on Tuesday in a luncheon organized by the merchant banking firm, Hamilton Pacific Holdings.
"I am here to knock the door of Wall Street," Mu said at the luncheon.

Inviting foreign financial companies to open representative offices and branches in Shenyang, Mu offered five years of local tax holidiay in addition to other incentives comparable to those offered by other Chinese cities.
Mu also proposed a new type of joint venture in which U.S. companies would assume management and complete control of one Chinese enterprise without putting in any capital.
The joint venture partners would split the profit at a pre-set ratio. If the enterprise fails to turn a profit, the loss would be shared by joint venture partners, he explained.
"This calls for minimal investment, minimal risk and greatest return," he said.

He said the city had many advantages vis-a-vis Shenzhen and Shanghai in the south, including its low-cost labor force, whose monthly wage averages 400 to 500 yuan. ($50 to $60; 8.29 yuan per U.S. dollar).
Mu said Shenyang has attracted $800 million in investments from some 400 U.S. companies.
